title: Stroke rehabilitation
what: Doctors, physical therapists, a speech therapist, and an occupational therapist help bring back movement, speech, and everyday skills.
why: After a stroke, as early as your doctor allows. Most recovery happens in the first months.
duration: sessions usually last 30 to 60 minutes; the course takes weeks to months, and continues at home
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially for blood pressure and blood thinners
Blood pressure, blood sugar, and heart
Joint pain, especially in the shoulder
Trouble swallowing, speaking, or with mood

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Comfortable sportswear and steady, closed shoes.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Take your medicines as usual. Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor, and they will decide.

prepare.title: Helper
prepare.text: It is good if someone close comes to sessions. They will learn how to help at home.

prepare.title: Goals
prepare.text: Think about what matters most to get back: walking, your hand, speech, self-care.

bring: Glasses or a hearing aid, if you use them
A cane or walker, if you have one
steps: The doctor examines you and sets goals together with you
Blood pressure and pulse are checked before the session
A physical therapist works on strength, balance, and walking
An occupational therapist trains daily skills: dressing, eating, washing
A speech therapist works on speech and swallowing, if needed
feel: Progress may be slow, but it shows over time
Sometimes it is emotionally hard. Tell your doctor. Help is available
after: Daily home exercises matter as much as the sessions
At home, remove rugs and cords you could trip on
Watch your blood pressure and take medicines as prescribed
Progress is checked regularly, and the program is adjusted
red_flags: New weakness in an arm or leg, a drooping face, or trouble speaking: call emergency services
A sudden severe headache or loss of consciousness: call emergency services
A fall with a blow to the head

faq.a: Usually in the first days in hospital, as soon as the doctor allows. The earlier, the better.
It varies. Most change happens in the first 3 to 6 months, but improvement can come later too.
Yes, and it matters. Your therapist will show you safe exercises.

reminders.text: Rehab session tomorrow. Bring comfortable clothes, shoes, and your medicine list.
